question: A 70-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes presents with malignant otitis externa. Granulation tissue is visible at the bony-cartilaginous junction of the left EAC. Radionuclide bone scan confirms skull base osteomyelitis. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate management priority?

answers.text: Prolonged systemic anti-pseudomonal antibiotic therapy (e.g., ciprofloxacin) and strict glycaemic control

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Systemic ciprofloxacin (oral or IV) targeting Pseudomonas aeruginosa, combined with tight glycaemic control, is the cornerstone of malignant OE management. Treatment duration is typically 6 to 8 weeks and is guided by serial imaging and ESR/CRP.

answers.text: Topical antibiotic-steroid ear drops and review in two weeks

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Topical drops alone are completely inadequate for malignant otitis externa with skull base involvement. Continued reliance on topical therapy is the classic error that leads to fatal disease progression.

answers.text: Immediate surgical debridement of the EAC and mastoidectomy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Surgical debridement has a very limited role in malignant OE; extensive surgery does not improve outcomes and carries high risk. Medical therapy with anti-pseudomonal antibiotics is the primary treatment.

answers.text: Aural toilet and topical acetic acid drops with outpatient follow-up

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Aural toilet and topical acetic acid are appropriate for simple diffuse otitis externa, not for malignant OE with skull base osteomyelitis. This approach is dangerous in confirmed malignant disease.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the management of malignant otitis externa. The cornerstone is prolonged systemic anti-pseudomonal therapy (ciprofloxacin) combined with strict glycaemic control. Topical drops are not sufficient and extensive surgery is not the primary approach.
Excellent. Systemic ciprofloxacin plus glycaemic control is the correct priority. Remember that malignant OE is primarily a medical emergency, not a surgical one.
